context.guidance: Do not write Personal Data or Authentication Secrets to localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies or outbound headers beyond what the session strictly needs. Keep identity in an opaque session identifier held server-side, and keep only non-Personal Data preferences in the browser. Where a value must be held client-side, protect it as Rule 6(1)(a) requires.

value.fix: Don't store the auth token in localStorage, because any script running on the page can read it there, and that includes an XSS payload. Have the server issue the session as an opaque session ID in a Set-Cookie header with the HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict (or Lax) flags, and keep all session and identity state on the server. On the client, delete `localStorage.setItem('token', data.token)`, stop returning the raw token in the JSON response body, and send requests with `credentials: 'include'` (fetch) or `withCredentials: true` (axios) so the browser attaches the cookie itself. Add CSRF protection, such as SameSite plus a CSRF token for state-changing requests. Clear any token already in localStorage with `localStorage.removeItem('token')`. Logout should invalidate the session on the server and clear the cookie. If a «SECRET» absolutely has to stay on the client, keep a short-lived access token in memory only (a JS variable, never Web Storage) and put the refresh token in an HttpOnly Secure cookie.
